page.layout: One block: a woodcut ornamental border across the top, then the title lines centred below it, in capitals. No running head, no page number visible in this part.; One page of text in a single column, with a woodcut historiated initial M at the upper left set into the text block; running head at the top; catchword-style signature line at the foot.

main_text.p: MUTUA animi cum corpore conjunctio est Unum ex primo notis, animus enim non aliunde institutus corpori suo quemlibet motum imperare assuescit; Id quod argumento est animo de sui cum corpore unione esse notitiam, quam aliunde non hauserit: Nec animus rebus delectabilibus suum admoveret corpus, ut inde suaviter ipse afficiatur, nisi & corpus sibi esse conjunctum sciret.
main_text.head: II.
main_text.p: Modus vero, quo animus unitus est corpori & vice versa, crucem figit omnibus Doctis; Ut mirandum non sit, quod Vir doctus, qui hanc conjunctionem nuper fuit diligentius meditatus, fatetur ideam modi, quo animus praesens est suo corpori, nobis esse nullam; Sic modum Gordianum, quo corpori mens est ligata, secavit, dum solvere non licuit.

page.notes: The woodcut border at the top is an ornament and carries no text. The fourth title line below "UNITUS CORPORI." is cut off at the bottom edge of this part, so it is not transcribed. The "De" line is in italic type. The initial letter of "QUO" and the "U" of "QUO" are set in the title's display capitals as printed. The woodcut initial M is described, not transcribed. The text is partly faded at the right edge. Several words are uncertain in the scan, notably "vice" and "Gordianum", and the catchword "III. Nec-" is printed as the last line.
